_comment: Board-specific config for imutag-smps, the switching-converter sibling of
This board is electrically identical to imutag-nand-bmp581 apart from the
power stage, so its settled positions apply here unchanged; see

analysis.track_in_git must be set here (it does not inherit), AND analysis/.gitignore must be left in place as a no-op file - analyze_pcb.py recreates an ignore-everything .gitignore whenever it is absent, without checking track_in_git.

notes: Switching-converter variant: TPS62840YBGR buck + 2.2 uH L1, versus the TPS7A02185 LDO on imutag-nand-bmp581. Everything else matches: same sensors, MCU, NAND, RTC, connectors and mounting holes.
Board is 21.5 x 11.5 mm, 4 layers, In1.Cu = +1V8 plane, In2.Cu = GND plane, ~0.38 mm stackup. copper_finish is still None - state it on the order.

power_profile.source: User-provided design intent, carried from imutag-nand-bmp581
power_profile.peak_condition: BMM350 flux-guide reset pulse from the CRST capacitor, <1 us, every ODR tick
notes: Expected average current is 1-2.2 mA. At 2 mA from 3.7 V the buck draws about 1.08 mA from the battery versus 2.00 mA for the LDO sibling - roughly 1.85x battery life. That advantage is NOT erased by forced PWM, because this package cannot be forced into PWM (see reviewer_notes).
TPS62840 quiescent current is 60 nA typical; switching frequency 1.8 MHz nominal, DCS-Control.
Analyzer heuristic power budgets are placeholders and meaningless here.

suppressions.reason: Low-power design at 1-2.2 mA average. 0.1016 mm traces are a fabrication process-selection concern, never a current-capacity one.
U5 LSM6DSV is used in SPI mode. The analyzer mistakes its dual-function pin names for an I2C bus.
Chip-select deselect is a firmware/reset-state contract using STM32 internal pull-ups.
BMM350 CRST is not a pull-up net. C4 = 2.2 uF from CRST to GND is the correct datasheet implementation.
VBAT is the external LiPo rail and VIN is the same net by design, inherited from a fixed interface.
J201 tag contacts are the production-test access method.
Connectors here are tag contacts, battery lands and mounting holes, not user cable interfaces.
J3xx are 1.1 mm mounting holes. J401 is a battery land, J201 a contact pad array.
/clkout is a 32 kHz RTC output, low risk.
Intentional compact 4-layer tag with In1.Cu = +1V8 and In2.Cu = GND.
No local datasheets/ directory by design; uses BoardDesigns/libraries/datasheets.
Fab-house panel fiducials are accepted for this flow.
Zero solder mask expansion is the KiCad default and the fab applies its own (~0.05 mm/side), giving NSMD lands.
GND vias inside GND exposed pads are the deliberate house pattern across the imutag family.

smps_architecture_2026_09_02: U4 is TPS62840YBGR, the WCSP-6 package. VSET tied directly to GND selects 1.8 V on the TPS62840YBG variant - confirmed against datasheet Table 1, first row '0.8 | 1.8 | 1.8 | 0 | GND | 0.01 k', the only row whose nominal resistance is GND. EN tied to VBAT keeps the rail always on.

CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL POINT: the YBG package has NO MODE pin. Datasheet section 8.3.3: 'This pin is not available in the YBG package, where the device automatically transitions between power-save and PWM modes.' Forced PWM is therefore unavailable on this variant.

Consequence: at 1-2.2 mA the converter sits in PFM, so switching noise is load-dependent, bursty and asynchronous with the BMM350's per-ODR-tick flux-guide reset - broadband and non-stationary rather than a filterable 1.8 MHz tone. It also means the buck keeps its full ~1.85x battery-life advantage, since the mode that would have erased it cannot be selected.

The family-level note in imutag-nand-bmp581 ('forced-mode SMPS efficiency is essentially LDO-like') evaluates an option this part does not offer. If a middle position is wanted it requires the SON-8 TPS62840DLC or an HVSSOP variant, which expose MODE at the cost of board area.

Magnetics split into two effects that must not be conflated: L1's metal-alloy core is a static soft-iron distorter 11.15 mm from U2 and IS calibratable (the 89-degree axis orientation already minimises it); the ripple-current field is time-varying, load-dependent and is NOT calibratable. Order-of-magnitude estimate for the latter is 0.01-0.1 uT against a 0.065 uT noise floor - a sanity check, not a specification, since turn count and ripple are assumed and Murata publishes no leakage figure for the DFE series.
switching_layout_verified_2026_09_02: SW node is 2.58 mm total, 2 segments, 0.254 mm wide, F.Cu only, no vias - short, wide and single-layer, which is what matters most.
C7 4.7 uF input cap is 1.60 mm from U4; L1 to C8 10 uF output is 2.24 mm; U4 to L1 is 3.39 mm.
Local F.Cu GND pour at U4, 2.80 x 1.29 mm at priority 2, with 4 GND vias within 2.9 mm, nearest at 1.15 mm.
F.Cu copper keepout under L1, 1.70 x 0.48 mm, keeping trace copper out from beneath the winding.
In2.Cu solid GND plane under the whole cluster, so return path sits directly beneath forward path.

LOW-SEVERITY OBSERVATION, improved by the 2026-09-02 reroute: /AT25_MOSI on B.Cu moved 1.13 -> 1.38 mm from L1's centre and is now clear of the 1.6 x 2.0 mm body outline; /AT25_SCK B.Cu 1.57 -> 1.69 mm, F.Cu unchanged at 1.59 mm. The seven vias within 3 mm did not move. The In2 GND plane sits between, giving real eddy-current shielding at 1.8 MHz, and flash traffic is intermittent. Not worth re-routing, but it is the first place to look if flash behaviour is marginal during heavy write bursts.
analysis_integrity: The 2026-08-26_0809 run was POISONED: its pcb.json named BitTagNG-LIS2DU12.kicad_pcb-back.kicad_pro as both project_settings.source and design_rule_compliance.rules_source, so Review 1's findings 7 and 8 (advanced process, edge clearance) were measured against another board's rules. That run has been PRUNED - the fact is recorded here so the finding is not re-derived from a file that no longer exists.

Caching propagates poison: a 2026-09-03_0646 run created by analyze_schematic.py alone carried the old pcb.json forward unchanged, still naming BitTagNG. Only a fresh analyze_pcb.py run (2026-09-03_0650) picked up imutag-smps.kicad_pro. After removing a stale project file, re-run the PCB analyzer explicitly - a schematic-only run will not clear it.
Current run 2026-09-03_0650 is correctly sourced to imutag-smps.kicad_pro and is the only one retained.
verified_correct_2026_09_02: KiCad DRC in the project directory: 0 violations, 0 unconnected, 0 parity.
Edge clearance and annular ring already fixed: inner copper 0.3005 mm from the profile, all 47 vias 0.5048/0.20 = 0.1524 mm (6.00 mil), single drill size.
The two ERC pin_to_pin warnings on U6 WP/HOLD against a power flag are the accepted pattern from Review 1.
open_items_2026_09_02: ARCHITECTURAL: decide deliberately whether PFM-only operation is acceptable, or move to a package exposing MODE. This is the one real question left.

Measure magnetometer noise against an assembled imutag-nand-bmp581 - the LDO sibling is the control experiment, so the comparison can be empirical rather than theoretical. Measure quiescent, 1 mA, and during a flash-write burst; a changing load is the interesting case because PFM burst rate moves with it.
copper_finish is None. Immersion silver reasoning from the sibling applies here with more force, since this board also has an inductor.
production_package_2026_09_02: Current export: pcbway_production/2026-09-03-07-51-02, verified against the board: 300/300 sampled fill vertices on both inner planes, 392/392 F.Cu+B.Cu segment starts, copper-to-edge 0.3005 mm, PTH 44 holes = 44 vias on a single 0.20 mm tool, BOM 16 lines / 27 placements matching the CPL exactly.

EXPORTS ALWAYS LOOK STALE - this is KiCad behaviour, not a problem. Exporting marks the board dirty, so it must be saved afterwards, which puts the .kicad_pcb mtime AFTER the export it produced. Every export in this board's history is seconds older than the board and every one matched. mtime carries no information here; verify by sampling zone-fill vertices and track-segment starts from the shipped Gerbers against the board file.
NOT ORDERED. The architectural question in finding 1 (PFM-only operation) is still undecided.
resolved_2026_09_02: BMP581 symbol updated from library: VSS pins 3/8/9 now power_in, matching libraries:BMP581. lib_symbol_mismatch cleared.

That update exposed power_pin_not_driven on U1 pin B1 (GND) - the same latent bug as RV-3028-C7-AccelTag on imutag-nand-bmp581, where a mistyped ground pin had been silently driving the GND net. The board's only PWR_FLAG was on a wire at (104.14, 21.59), not GND. Resolved by adding #FLG02 coincident with the GND symbol at (20.32, 66.04).
L1 reroute: /AT25_MOSI B.Cu moved 1.13 -> 1.38 mm from L1 centre, now clear of the 1.6 x 2.0 mm body outline.
The GND fix is real: with all ERC exclusions cleared, the U1 Pin B1 [GND] power_pin_not_driven error is gone.

2026-09-03 load-switch removal verified: DRC 0 violations; ERC 0 errors with all 24 exclusions cleared; 33 footprints / 27 placements; 44 vias all at 6.00 mil; copper-to-edge 0.3005 mm; verified against the export current at the time (since pruned); the retained export is 2026-09-03-07-51-02.
review_process_traps: DO NOT simulate an ERC or DRC change on a copy of the project - verify in the board's own directory. On 2026-09-02 a BMP581 symbol update was reported as 'verified safe' from a copy whose symbol libraries did not resolve; applying it for real produced a power_pin_not_driven error. The tell was that lib_symbol_mismatch persisted in the test even after the symbols were made to match, which meant the comparison was not running. The same trap already applies to DRC, where a copy without fp-lib-table yields phantom lib_footprint_issues.

The helpers read analysis/*/schematic.json, which is a SNAPSHOT. On 2026-09-03 the newest run was 190 hours old and still contained the removed load switch, so stm32_pinmap.py would have reported the previous revision and looked entirely plausible. _common.load now warns loudly when the analysis predates the design file. Re-run analyze_schematic.py after any schematic change.

analysis/.gitignore is recreated by analysis_cache.py whenever the BOARD's .kicad-happy.json has track_in_git false or ABSENT. It does not inherit from BoardDesigns/.kicad-happy.json. Trimming a board config to 'inherit' that setting silently re-ignores the analysis directory on the next analyzer run - which happened here on 2026-09-03. Set analysis.track_in_git explicitly in every board config.

Check every lib_id prefix a schematic uses appears in that project's own sym-lib-table. A prefix resolved only by the user-level table (~/Library/Preferences/kicad/<ver>/sym-lib-table) works on the authoring machine and fails on a fresh clone, while ERC stays clean because the cached lib_symbols entry hides it. Found on imutag-smps 2026-09-03 with tag_library:RV-3028-C7.
erc_exclusions_2026_09_02: ERC reports 0 violations with 24 erc_exclusions in .kicad_pro (20 pin_to_pin, 2 multiple_net_names, 1 lib_symbol_mismatch, 1 power_pin_not_driven). They live in .kicad_pro, not the gitignored .kicad_prl, so they travel with the repo.

RESOLVED 2026-09-02: #FLG01 was moved from /Flash 1V8 to +1V8. With ALL exclusions cleared the board now shows 0 errors and 8 warnings, down from 2 errors and 9 warnings. Both former errors - power_pin_not_driven on U1 pin A2 [VIN] and the U1 VOUT / #FLG01 Output-to-Power-output conflict - are gone.
Some of the 24 exclusions are now stale, matching nothing. Harmless, but they could be pruned.
'ERC clean' still means 'clean given accepted exclusions'; the reasons live here.
af_verification_2026_09_02: AF data now comes from the STM32_open_pin_data submodule (ST's machine-readable pin data, the STM32CubeMX source), not the datasheet PDF. Generate with: python3 BoardDesigns/kicad-helpers/af_tables/generate.py STM32U375KGUx

Cross-checked against a careful by-hand read of DS14861 Rev 3 Tables 22-23: 48/54 entries agree, the six differences being label style only (DEBUG_JTMS-SWDIO vs JTMS/SWDIO, RCC_MCO vs MCO). No substantive disagreement - but the XML has no column-shift failure mode, so it is the source of record.

ST's pin positions independently confirm the KiCad symbol's pin numbering: all 25 GPIO positions match the netlist. That is the automated form of 'verify pinouts against the manufacturer, never the symbol'.
Derived from the same data: PC14 has no peripheral AF at all (only EVENTOUT) so using it costs the LSE; PB3 forfeits JTDO-SWO and PB4 forfeits NJTRST on AF0.

CORRECTION: an earlier pass called PC14 a plain GPIO that 'costs you the LSE' and claimed the accurate 32 kHz could not reach LPTIM1. Both wrong, same root cause - the check read only ALTERNATE functions and ignored ADDITIONAL functions, so RCC_OSC32_IN was invisible. The clock reaches LPTIM1 via the RCC tree, not an LPTIM input pin. generate.py now captures an 'additional' map and the helper reports it.
resolved_2026_09_03: All 12 U302 pin alternates declared on the schematic, including PC14 -> RCC_OSC32_IN. stm32_pinmap.py reads them from the .kicad_sch, so pin intent is stated by the design rather than inferred.
RV-3028 CLKOUT retyped input -> output in tag_library and the schematic cache. Correct direction (the RTC drives) and required for coherence with PC14 declaring RCC_OSC32_IN.
TPS22916BYFPR lib_symbol_mismatch is moot - U1 went with the load switch, no orphan lib_symbols entry remains.

U501 repointed tag_library:RV-3028-C7 -> libraries:RV-3028-C7. 'tag_library' is not in this project's sym-lib-table and resolved only via the user-level table, so the reference was machine-local. Connectivity verified unchanged: 37 nets, 138 pin connections.
ERC exclusions 24 -> 17 (seven retired with the load switch); 0 errors with all cleared.

DRC rule severities tightened: npth_inside_courtyard and pth_inside_courtyard ignore -> warning, and track_not_centered_on_via ignore -> ERROR. Board passes with them active. The third matters here because the design was moved to a 6.00 mil annular ring for margin, and an off-centre track endpoint would give some of that back silently.
BMP581 symbol updated from library and now in sync - pin maps identical, VSS pins 3/8/9 power_in.
known_false_positives: missing_courtyard is set to ignore deliberately. Promoting it yields exactly five hits - J301-J304 (1.1 mm mounting holes) and J401 (battery lands) - none of which are placed components with spacing constraints. Verified in place 2026-09-03; the setting conceals no real overlap risk.

mating_design.name: imutag-smps self-contained tag
notes: AF CROSS-CHECK (DS14861 Rev 3, Tables 22-23): the /LPS_* group is NOT a second SPI bus. PA11 = SPI1_MISO and PA12 = SPI1_MOSI on AF5 - the SAME peripheral signals as PA6/PA7 - and PB3 = SPI1_SCK on AF5, same as PA5. Across AF0-AF15 PA11's only other peripheral is FDCAN1_RX and PA12's is FDCAN1_TX, so there is no alternative. SPI3 is not an escape route either: PB3 offers SPI3_SCK on AF6, but SPI3_MISO is PB4 and SPI3_MOSI is PB5, both wired to /LSM_TRG and /BMM_INT. Firmware must either remap SPI1 pins at runtime when switching between the flash/IMU group and the BMP581, or bit-bang the BMP581 bus. Not a board defect - but firmware written assuming two independent hardware SPI buses will not work.

Two separate SPI buses: U5 LSM6DSV and U6 NAND share /AT25_SCK, /AT25_MISO, /AT25_MOSI on PA5-PA7 with independent selects (PA4 = /AT25_nCS for the NAND, PB1 = /LSM_CS for the IMU). U3 BMP581 has its own bus, /LPS_* on PA9-PA12 and PB3. No external pull-ups on either, so deselect is a reset-state and first-GPIO-action firmware contract.
PB7 is BOOT0 and carries /SDA with a 10 kOhm pull-up to +1V8, so the strap is high at reset. Production programming MUST write and read back the option bytes.
Six GPIOs unused - PC15, PA1, PA2, PA3, PB0, PA15. Configure analog/no-pull for lowest leakage. PA15 has a default pull-up on STM32 and is the one most worth setting explicitly.
NRST is transistor-driven via Q501 collector with C502.
PB3 AF0 is JTDO/TRACESWO, given up for /LPS_CK - so no SWO trace. SWD on PA13/PA14 unaffected. PB4 AF0 is NJTRST, given up for /LSM_TRG, irrelevant under SWD.

32 kHz TIMEBASE CHAIN: U501 RV-3028 CLKOUT (32.768 kHz, 1 PPM) -> PC14/OSC32_IN with the LSE in BYPASS mode -> LPTIM1 -> divided -> PB4/LPTIM1_CH2 (AF1) -> U5 LSM6DSV trigger. The LSM samples on a hardware schedule while the CPU is stopped, and the interval inherits the RTC's 1 PPM accuracy. No crystal anywhere on the tag. PC14 has no ALTERNATE functions but ST lists RCC_OSC32_IN as an ADDITIONAL function (peripheral registers, not GPIOx_AFR). PB4 is NOT a GPIO. The alternative LPTIM1_CH2 pin is PA1, unused, so nothing is contended.

2026-09-03: the TPS22916 load switch (U1) and its decoupling (C10, C507) were REMOVED - measured benefit was negligible. U6 NAND VCC now sits directly on +1V8; the /Flash 1V8 and /FLASH_PWR nets no longer exist; PA8 is unconnected and is now the seventh unused GPIO. The NAND's standby current is drawn continuously, which is the measured trade - do not re-add a load switch on theory. Re-measure if the deployment duty cycle changes.

host_pin_map.function: RV-3028 CLKOUT into LSE bypass, 1 PPM MCU timebase
host_pin_map.af: RCC_OSC32_IN additional function - LSE bypass input
no SPI AF exists - GPIO is correct
no SPI_NSS exists - GPIO is correct
AF5 SPI1_SCK - COLLIDES with PA5 (AF6 = SPI3_SCK, unusable here)
AF1 LPTIM1_CH2 - divided 32 kHz LSM trigger (forfeits NJTRST)

host_pin_map.port: PC15, PA1, PA2, PA3, PB0, PA8, PA15
host_pin_map.function: UNUSED (7) - set analog/no-pull for lowest leakage; PA8 freed by the load-switch removal
